reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate and adds shared predicates (isSkippedDay, isWeekendSkippedDaily, getWeekdayCycleLength) in shared/schedules.ts, but the new getDatesInRange rebuilds getUpcomingDates' occurrence pipeline instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: The 'daily: filter skipped days, otherwise move with getDateWithSkippedWeekend' dispatch is written out separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and twice in schedule-template.ts, and getWeekendShiftDays parallels getWeekdayCycleLength as a second ad-hoc window formula.

placement.why: Day predicates and the solve loop live in shared/schedules.ts, the new handler sits next to getUpcomingDates in schedules/app.ts, and the RecurConfig type gains holidays; the window helper living only in the server module is a minor split.

scope.why: Covers the four requested behaviours; passing frequency through parseRecurDate is needed for the daily rule; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Holiday matching is defined once in isSkippedDay, but how an occurrence becomes a final day (skip vs move, window sizes) is decided at five call sites with growing '&& !isWeekendSkipping' conditions, so the next rule change must again touch them all.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Sites use the existing getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend and the new shared predicates; the problem is repeated dispatch around them rather than going around an existing abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange is a reshaped copy of getUpcomingDates' occurrences/filter/map pipeline (range bounds and dedupe added), and getWeekendShiftDays is a second variant of the getWeekdayCycleLength search-window formula.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-skip branch (wider take window, candidate search) and a '!skipsWeekendDays' guard; schedule-template.ts (two blocks), getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each re-implement the skip-vs-move decision instead of one shared resolver.
